description: Only PRIJEM (positive) and VYDAJ (negative) give a signed amount; VYBER transactions are left out of the signed-amount average.

c.request: Linking each transaction to its account (skipping transactions without one), for each account statement frequency work out the average signed transaction amount — credits ('PRIJEM') positive, withdrawals negative, and any transaction that is neither left out — along with the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep the frequencies above it, and give me one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean. Don't round. Only PRIJEM (positive) and VYDAJ (negative) give a signed amount; VYBER transactions are left out of the signed-amount average.
c.sql:
WITH per_frequency AS (
    SELECT
        a.frequency,
        AVG(CASE
                WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount
            END) AS avg_signed_amount,
        AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
mean_signed AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_signed_amount
    FROM per_frequency
)
SELECT
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount) AS average_signed_average,
    AVG(p.avg_balance) AS average_balance_average,
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount - m.mean_signed_amount) AS average_excess
FROM per_frequency AS p
CROSS JOIN mean_signed AS m
WHERE p.avg_signed_amount > m.mean_signed_amount;

b.request: Join each transaction to its account, excluding transactions without a matching account; group by account statement frequency and calculate the average signed amount using PRIJEM as positive and VYDAJ as negative, excluding all other transaction types including VYBER, plus the average post-transaction balance. Take the unweighted mean of the per-frequency signed averages, retain frequencies whose signed average is above that mean, and return one row with the unweighted averages of their signed averages, balance averages, and signed-average excesses over the mean, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH per_frequency AS (
    SELECT a.frequency,
           AVG(CASE t.type
                   WHEN 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                   WHEN 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount
               END) AS avg_signed_amount,
           AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    WHERE t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ')
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
frequency_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_signed_amount
    FROM per_frequency
)
SELECT AVG(p.avg_signed_amount) AS avg_signed_amount,
       AVG(p.avg_balance) AS avg_balance,
       AVG(p.avg_signed_amount - m.mean_signed_amount) AS avg_signed_amount_excess
FROM per_frequency AS p
CROSS JOIN frequency_mean AS m
WHERE p.avg_signed_amount > m.mean_signed_amount;

a.request: Joining each transaction to its account (dropping transactions with no matching account), compute for each account statement frequency (`account.frequency`) the average signed transaction amount — `trans.amount` taken as positive when `trans.type` is 'PRIJEM', negative when it is 'VYDAJ', and left out (no value) for every other type, including 'VYBER' — and the average `trans.balance` over all its transactions. Then take the plain mean of those per-frequency average signed amounts, keep only the frequencies whose average signed amount is above that mean, and return a single row with: the average of their average signed amounts, the average of their average balances, and the average of how far their average signed amount exceeds the mean. Don't round.
a.sql:
WITH per_frequency AS (
    SELECT
        a.frequency,
        AVG(CASE
                WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount
                WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount
                ELSE NULL
            END) AS avg_signed_amount,
        AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
mean_signed AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_signed_amount) AS mean_avg_signed_amount
    FROM per_frequency
)
SELECT
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount) AS average_of_above_mean_signed_amounts,
    AVG(p.avg_balance) AS average_of_above_mean_balances,
    AVG(p.avg_signed_amount - m.mean_avg_signed_amount) AS average_excess_signed_amount
FROM per_frequency AS p
CROSS JOIN mean_signed AS m
WHERE p.avg_signed_amount > m.mean_avg_signed_amount;

d.request: Link each transaction to its account, skipping transactions without one. For each account statement frequency, calculate the average signed transaction amount, treating `PRIJEM` as positive and `VYDAJ` as negative; exclude all other transaction types from this average. Also calculate the average balance after the transaction for each frequency. Take the simple mean of the per-frequency signed averages, keep frequencies whose signed average is above that mean, and return one row with the average of those frequencies’ signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed averages exceed the mean. Do not round.
d.sql:
WITH frequency_averages AS (
    SELECT
        a.frequency,
        AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS signed_avg,
        AVG(t.balance) AS balance_avg
    FROM trans AS t
    JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
    GROUP BY a.frequency
),
above_mean AS (
    SELECT frequency, signed_avg, balance_avg
    FROM frequency_averages
    WHERE signed_avg > (SELECT AVG(signed_avg) FROM frequency_averages)
)
SELECT
    AVG(signed_avg) AS average_signed_transaction_amount,
    AVG(balance_avg) AS average_balance,
    AVG(signed_avg - (SELECT AVG(signed_avg) FROM frequency_averages)) AS average_excess_over_mean
FROM above_mean;
